model.name: AI Model Evaluation
model.purpose: Govern the dataset, metric, run, finding and approval lifecycle used to test, evaluate, verify and validate an AI model or AI system, independently of storage format or access interface.
model.scope_statement: This aggregate covers an evaluation campaign from stated claims and acceptance criteria through bound evaluation datasets and splits, metric and metrology-block definitions, executable tasks and adaptation protocols, runs and sandboxed environments, sample-level scoring and judging, aggregate results with uncertainty, findings against claims, and gated approval, re-evaluation and evidence packaging. Dataset catalogues and model artifacts are referenced, not owned. JSON logs, YAML tasks, Markdown reports, Git trees, MCP tools and MongoDB collections are projections of these semantics, not the model.
in_scope: Evaluation campaign identity, purpose, intended operational context and risk class of the evaluation itself
Claims, hypotheses, acceptance thresholds and go or no-go criteria under test
Binding of a versioned evaluation dataset, split, sample frame and ground-truth or target labels as used in a campaign
Metric, scorer, metrology-block, event and tool definitions including multi-metric and human or model-as-judge schemes
Task, scenario and adaptation or prompting protocols that convert a general model into a scenario-specific system under test
Evaluation-run execution, environment, sandbox, limits, epochs, retries and run status
Sample-level outputs, scores, reductions, refusals, integrity scans and aggregate metrics with uncertainty
Evaluation findings, limitations, incompleteness disclosures and evidence packs
Approval, rejection, waiver and conformity-assessment decisions that consume evaluation evidence
Post-market, continuous and triggered re-evaluation, including feedback-loop monitoring for systems that keep learning
Roles, ownership, independence of validators from builders, access, retention, deletion and reproducibility packaging
Alignment of evaluation practice to TEVV, classification-performance assessment, accuracy and robustness declaration, and dataset-split metadata
out_of_scope: Canonical identity, licensing, record schema and publication of a benchmark dataset as a catalogue object, which belongs to WM-AI-009
Identity, weights, training run, architecture and release of the model artifact under test, which belongs to WM-SFT-004
Enterprise AI risk-management policy, risk inventory and residual-risk acceptance outside the Measure or TEVV evidence path
Serious-incident investigation, market-surveillance casework and fundamental-rights impact assessment as standalone governance objects
Training-data acquisition, labelling operations and training-set quality except insofar as they are controls against evaluation leakage
Inference serving, prompt-routing products and general software-quality testing of non-AI components
Sector-specific clinical, credit or safety-case methods that are not evaluation of an AI model or system

boundary_notes.distinction: WM-AI-009 is the reusable dataset object (identity, Croissant description, license, files, recordsets, splits as published). This model only binds a named dataset version and split into a campaign, records sampling, contamination controls and evaluation-time usage, and must not duplicate dataset master data.

WM-SFT-004 is the subject under evaluation. This model records which artifact version, interface and generation configuration were assessed, and must not store weights, training hyperparameters or model-card identity as if they were evaluation objects.

boundary_notes.neighbor: NIST AI RMF Govern, Map and Manage functions
boundary_notes.distinction: Evaluation implements Measure and TEVV. Organizational risk appetite, context mapping and risk treatment live in the risk-management neighbor; this model consumes Map context and emits evidence for Manage, including go or no-go decisions.

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISO/IEC 22989 AI concepts and ISO/IEC 23053 ML system framework
boundary_notes.distinction: Those standards define AI system, model, training, validation and testing data, and lifecycle vocabulary. This model uses that vocabulary for evaluation datasets and subjects but does not redefine the AI system itself. ISO/IEC TS 4213 normatively references ISO/IEC 22989 and explicitly excludes benchmarking and application use cases, which this model covers by alignment to HELM, Inspect and TEVV-Athlon rather than by claiming 4213 conformance for those parts.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Software testing of AI-based systems (ISO/IEC TR 29119-11 and ISO/IEC TS 42119-2)
boundary_notes.distinction: Those documents address test oracles, black-box and white-box testing and test environments for systems that contain AI. This model covers the evaluation campaign, metrics, runs and approvals; it does not own general test-process, test-item or defect-management semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Formal robustness assessment of neural networks (ISO/IEC 24029 series)
boundary_notes.distinction: Formal, statistical and empirical robustness methods are neighboring measurement techniques. This model can record that a robustness event used such a method; it does not encode solvers, reachability proofs or perturbation algebras. Primary text for 24029 was not fully retrieved in this research pass and is treated as an alignment gap.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Defines Measure and TEVV as the evaluation function, trustworthy characteristics, separation of builders from validators, scientific-integrity and construct-validation expectations, and go or no-go commissioning decisions.

sources.title: The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems, NIST AI 200-2 ipd
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.version_or_date: NIST AI 200-2 ipd, August 2026 (comment period through 2026-10-06)
sources.relevance: Four-stage evaluation design (Articulate and Organize, Define and Construct, Apply and Measure, Synthesize and Interrogate); metrology blocks, events and tools; benchmarks, red teaming and field testing; Goodhart caution; TEVV-Athlon as the Measure implementation.

sources.title: ISO/IEC TS 4213:2022 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Assessment of machine learning classification performance
sources.relevance: Normative process and control criteria for classification performance assessment, including representativeness, leakage, ground truth, evaluation environment, baselines, confusion-matrix metrics, computational complexity and statistical significance tests. Explicitly does not address benchmarking or use cases.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.relevance: Article 15 accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity including declared accuracy metrics, lifecycle consistency, feedback loops and adversarial or poisoning attacks; Articles 10, 43, 55, 72 and 92 for datasets, conformity assessment, GPAI systemic-risk evaluation, post-market monitoring and official evaluations.

sources.title: Croissant Format Specification 1.1
sources.relevance: Dataset identity, FileObject integrity hashes, RecordSet fields, training/validation/test splits, PROV-O provenance and license metadata used when binding evaluation datasets without copying dataset-master semantics.

sources.title: Inspect AI: Framework for Large Language Model Evaluations
sources.version_or_date: Software citation May 2024; documentation accessed 2026-08-26 including eval-logs and scoring pages
sources.relevance: Operational information model of a Task as dataset plus solver plus scorer; EvalLog fields (status, eval, plan, results, stats, samples, reductions); scoring, model grading, scanners, sandboxes and re-scoring workflow.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
sources.organization: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
sources.relevance: Scenario as task, domain and language; multi-metric measurement in the same context; standardized adaptation; explicit incompleteness of coverage; trade-offs among accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity and efficiency.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, NIST AI 600-1
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Cross-sector generative-AI profile of AI RMF for design, development, use and evaluation of GAI, including GAI-specific risks that evaluation campaigns must map to metrics and events.

sources.title: ISO/IEC TR 29119-11:2020 Software and systems engineering — Software testing — Part 11: Guidelines on the testing of AI-based systems
sources.relevance: Test-oracle problem, non-determinism, acceptance-criteria difficulty, black-box and neural-network white-box testing, test environments and lifecycle testing of AI-based systems.

sources.title: Autonomous Systems Evaluation Standard
sources.relevance: Minimum quality bar for submitting evaluations: Inspect-based implementation, repository structure, and recommended binary success metric as main scorer for autonomous-system tasks.

bundles.name: Campaign scope and subject
bundles.description: Identity of the evaluation campaign, the claims and acceptance criteria it tests, the AI model or system version under test, and the class of evaluation being performed.
bundles.rationale: NIST TEVV-Athlon Stage 1 requires a jargon-free evaluation goal and stakeholder use of results. AI RMF Measure consumes Map context and produces go or no-go evidence. HELM treats the model, not a scenario-specific fine-tune, as the object of evaluation when adaptation is controlled.

layers.name: Campaign definition
layers.description: Master identity, purpose, claims and thresholds that make an evaluation campaign a governed object rather than an ad hoc script run.

findings.name: Evaluation campaign identity
findings.description: A campaign is the governed aggregate that groups one or more tasks, datasets, metrics, runs and later findings against a stated goal. Inspect writes one EvalLog per task evaluated; TEVV-Athlon requires organizers to state goals, stakeholders, time, cost and success conditions before constructing blocks and events.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier does the evaluation platform of record assign to this campaign, and which governed IRI or Dimension UUID or ULID is used if the master system has none?
What is the evaluation goal in non-jargon terms, who will use the results, and what decision will the results change?

Is this campaign a standardized benchmark comparison, red-team or adversarial event, human or field test, conformity-assessment test, post-market monitor, or a composed TEVV-Athlon of several event types?
What is the campaign lifecycle state (planned, in execution, scored, synthesized, approved, superseded or withdrawn) and which event times mark each transition?

data_elements.name: Campaign master identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the evaluation platform of record; not a date.

data_elements.name: Campaign IRI
data_elements.description: Governed global identifier when the adopting Dimension publishes the campaign.

data_elements.name: Goal statement
data_elements.description: Concise evaluation objective without unexplained jargon.

data_elements.name: Evaluation class
data_elements.description: Coded class such as benchmark, red-team, field-test, conformity, post-market or composite.

data_elements.name: Campaign state
data_elements.description: Lifecycle state of the campaign aggregate.

artifacts.name: Evaluation plan
artifacts.description: Serial plan capturing goal, stakeholders, resources, event types, independence of validators and intended evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system campaign identifier, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID; plan revision is a serial, not an identity.

findings.name: Claims and acceptance criteria
findings.description: The testable claims, performance or trustworthiness characteristics, thresholds and go or no-go rules that scoring and findings will be judged against. EU Article 15 requires declared accuracy metrics and lifecycle-consistent performance; AI RMF expects explicit commissioning decisions and construct validation of TEVV parameters.

questions.text: Which claims, trustworthiness characteristics or metrology blocks are under test, and how is each claim stated so a finding can be true, false or inconclusive?
What quantitative or qualitative acceptance thresholds, including uncertainty bounds, must be met for a pass, and who authorized those thresholds?
What go, no-go, waive or conditional-deploy rule will be applied to aggregated findings, and which residual risks remain acceptable if the rule fires?
Must accuracy or other performance levels be declared in instructions for use or technical documentation, and which metrics are the declared ones?

data_elements.name: Claim identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of a testable claim within the campaign.

data_elements.name: Claim text
data_elements.description: Falsifiable statement the evaluation can support, refute or leave inconclusive.

data_elements.name: Acceptance threshold
data_elements.description: Numeric or coded pass criterion including comparator and optional uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Gate rule
data_elements.description: Decision procedure mapping findings to go, no-go, waive or conditional deploy.

artifacts.name: Claims and thresholds register
artifacts.description: Versioned register of claims, characteristics, declared metrics and gate rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Campaign master identifier plus claim-register serial; each claim has its own identifier.

layers.name: Subject under evaluation
layers.description: The model or system version, interface and generation configuration being assessed, kept distinct from the evaluation campaign.

findings.name: Subject under evaluation
findings.description: HELM standardizes adaptation so the object of evaluation is the language model rather than a scenario-specific system. Inspect EvalSpec records task, model and creation time. AI RMF separates actors who build and use models from those who verify and validate them. The subject is a reference to WM-SFT-004 plus the exact interface used at evaluation time.

questions.text: Which model or AI-system artifact identifier, version and interface (API, checkpoint, agent bridge) is the subject under evaluation?
What generation, decoding, tool-use, temperature and context-window configuration was frozen for this campaign so results are attributable to the subject rather than to an uncontrolled adapter?
Were the actors who built or operate the subject separated from the actors who designed, executed or scored the evaluation, and if not what conflict is recorded?
Is the subject open-weight, limited-access API or closed, and how does that access class constrain reproducibility and third-party re-run rights?

data_elements.name: Subject artifact identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the WM-SFT-004 artifact under test.

data_elements.name: Subject version
data_elements.description: Exact version, snapshot or model-id string used at evaluation time.

data_elements.name: Generation configuration
data_elements.description: Frozen decoding, tool and context settings that define the evaluated interface.

data_elements.name: Validator independence status
data_elements.description: Coded separation of builders from validators.

artifacts.name: Subject binding record
artifacts.description: Record pinning the evaluated artifact version, interface and generation configuration.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Campaign master identifier plus subject artifact identifier and version; not a date.

bundles.name: Evaluation design assets
bundles.description: Datasets as used, split and leakage controls, metrics and metrology blocks, scenarios, tasks and adaptation protocols that make runs comparable.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC TS 4213 requires control criteria before metric computation. Croissant supplies split and integrity metadata for the bound dataset. HELM taxonomizes scenarios and metrics and demands standardized adaptation. TEVV-Athlon Define and Construct turns goals into blocks; Apply and Measure selects events and tools.

layers.name: Datasets, splits and integrity
layers.description: How an evaluation dataset is bound, split, sampled and protected from leakage and contamination.

findings.name: Evaluation dataset binding
findings.description: Inspect Tasks load labelled samples with input and target fields from Hugging Face, CSV, JSON or in-memory sources. Croissant describes FileObject sha256, RecordSet keys and cr:TrainingSplit, cr:ValidationSplit and cr:TestSplit. This finding binds a dataset version into the campaign; master dataset description remains WM-AI-009. EU Article 10 distinguishes training, validation and testing datasets for high-risk systems.

questions.text: Which dataset master identifier, version, split and Croissant or equivalent description is bound as the evaluation set, and is that binding a test split rather than training data?
What is the target or ground-truth field, who authored the labels, and what annotation protocol or inter-rater evidence supports those labels?
What license and usage restrictions apply to evaluation-time use, redistribution of prompts or publication of sample-level outputs?
Is the bound dataset live or frozen, and if live how is the exact snapshot used by a run identified?

data_elements.name: Dataset master identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to WM-AI-009 or other dataset of record.

data_elements.name: Split code
data_elements.description: Training, validation, test or custom split used for this binding.

data_elements.name: Target field
data_elements.description: Field holding the ideal answer, grade rubric or ground truth.

data_elements.name: Content integrity hash
data_elements.description: SHA-256 or equivalent of bound files when available from Croissant FileObject.

artifacts.name: Dataset binding record
artifacts.description: Pin of dataset version, split, hashes, license and sample-field map used by the campaign.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset master identifier plus version and split code, referenced from the campaign master identifier.

findings.name: Split leakage and contamination controls
findings.description: ISO/IEC TS 4213 control criteria include representativeness and bias, preprocessing, test and validation data, cross-validation, limiting information leakage and channel effects, and ground truth. HELM and Inspect scanners additionally treat evaluation awareness, refusals and environment misconfiguration as threats to result validity.

questions.text: What controls prevent training-set overlap, prompt leakage, canary exposure or use of the test split during development of the subject?
How was the sample frame shown to be representative of the intended operational domain, and which groups or languages are known to be missing?
Were transcripts or items scanned for evaluation awareness, memorization of test items or harness artifacts, and what was the outcome?
Where expected results are unavailable or non-deterministic, how is the test oracle defined so pass and fail remain decidable?

data_elements.name: Leakage control status
data_elements.description: Coded result of overlap and leakage checks.

data_elements.name: Known coverage gaps
data_elements.description: Scenarios, languages or groups explicitly missing, per HELM incompleteness principle.

data_elements.name: Oracle type
data_elements.description: Gold label, heuristic match, human judge, model judge, sandbox property or mixed.

artifacts.name: Contamination and leakage report
artifacts.description: Evidence of split hygiene, overlap checks, canaries and scanner results.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Campaign master identifier plus contamination-report serial.

layers.name: Metrics, tasks and adaptation
layers.description: What is measured, on which scenarios, with which adaptation of the general model.

findings.name: Metric and metrology-block definition
findings.description: ISO/IEC TS 4213 specifies confusion-matrix base elements and derived metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Hamming loss, Jaccard, latency, throughput, energy) plus significance tests. HELM requires multi-metric measurement in the same scenario. TEVV-Athlon Blocks are the concepts or metrics the evaluation aims to assess and must include a precise definition of required evidence. Inspect scorers emit Score values aggregated by metrics such as accuracy or mean, with optional clustered standard errors.

questions.text: What is the exact metric definition, unit, aggregation (micro, macro, weighted, sample-mean, clustered) and direction of goodness?

Which metrics are measured on the same scenario so accuracy is not the sole reported desideratum, and which HELM-class metrics (calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency) are absent?
What construct-validation argument shows that this metric measures the intended trustworthiness characteristic rather than a Goodhart proxy?
What statistical test, confidence interval or clustered-error method will be used to compare systems or detect change, and is the analysis pre-registered?

data_elements.name: Metric identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of a metric or scorer-metric pair.

data_elements.name: Metric formula or scorer reference
data_elements.description: Definition sufficient to recompute the metric from sample scores.

data_elements.name: Aggregation method
data_elements.description: How sample scores reduce to a campaign result, including multi-epoch reductions.

data_elements.name: Metrology block identifier
data_elements.description: TEVV-Athlon Block this metric evidences.

artifacts.name: Metric specification
artifacts.description: Versioned specification of metric, scorer, aggregation, construct and significance plan.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Metric identifier in the evaluation platform of record, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Scenario, task and adaptation protocol
findings.description: A HELM scenario is a task plus domain plus language. Inspect Task composes dataset, solver or agent, and scorer, optionally with a sandbox and tools. Standardized few-shot or other adaptation is required so comparisons attribute performance to the subject. UK AISI autonomous-system submissions must be Inspect tasks and should expose a binary success scorer.

questions.text: What task, domain, language or modality, and user-facing use case define this scenario, and which HELM or Inspect eval identifier does it correspond to?
What adaptation protocol (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, agent loop, tool use) is frozen, including prompt templates and in-context example policy?
If the task is agentic, which tools, MCP servers and sandbox (Docker, Kubernetes or other) isolate untrusted model actions, and what approval gates exist for tool calls?
Does the scenario depend on a geographic, legal or language locale, and if so which locale constraints apply to items and raters?

data_elements.name: Scenario identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the task-domain-language triple or Inspect task name.

data_elements.name: Adaptation kind
data_elements.description: Coded adaptation strategy frozen for comparability.

data_elements.name: Sandbox kind
data_elements.description: Isolation mechanism for untrusted code or tool use, if any.

artifacts.name: Task and adaptation specification
artifacts.description: Inspect-style or equivalent task definition: dataset map, solver, scorer, sandbox and prompts.
media_or_form: source projection such as Python module
artifacts.identity_strategy: Task or scenario identifier from the evaluation platform of record; prompt and solver revisions are serials.

bundles.name: Execution and scoring
bundles.description: Runs, environments, sample-level scoring, model grading, human judging and integrity events that turn a design into evidence.
bundles.rationale: Inspect EvalLog is the de facto run record (status, plan, samples, scores, stats, errors). TEVV-Athlon Apply and Measure collects evidence with events and tools. ISO/IEC TS 4213 requires a documented evaluation environment and appropriate baselines.

layers.name: Run and environment
layers.description: Executable evaluation runs, their status, environment, limits and resource stats.

findings.name: Evaluation run
findings.description: Every inspect eval or equivalent execution writes a log with status started, success or error, EvalSpec, EvalPlan, EvalStats (token usage), optional EvalError, tags, metadata and sample list. Location is a URI (file, S3 or other). Failed runs may be retried. Event time of inference differs from ingestion time of the log.

questions.text: What master-system run identifier, log URI and status (started, success, error, aborted, retried) identify this execution?
When did the run start and end as event time, and when was the log ingested, each in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset?
What evaluation environment, hardware, software versions, seeds, parallelism, epoch count and cost or energy envelope were used?
Which error-handling, sample limits, timeouts or early-stopping rules fired, and is the result a partial run?

data_elements.name: Run master identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the evaluation platform of record for this execution.

data_elements.name: Log location URI
data_elements.description: Storage URI of the EvalLog or equivalent run record.

data_elements.name: Run status
data_elements.description: started, success, error or equivalent.

data_elements.name: Run started at
data_elements.description: Event time the run began, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

data_elements.name: Usage statistics
data_elements.description: Input and output token counts or analogous resource stats.

artifacts.name: Evaluation run log
artifacts.description: Authoritative run record containing spec, plan, samples, scores, stats and errors. Media may be .eval binary or JSON projection; semantics are the log object, not the file type.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system run identifier and log URI; file format is a projection.

layers.name: Scoring and judging
layers.description: Conversion of raw model output into scores, including deferred scoring, model grading and human raters.

findings.name: Scoring and judging
findings.description: Inspect scoring maps output to a Score against a Target, with built-in match, multiple-choice, math, model-graded and perplexity scorers, custom scorers, multiple scorers and epoch reductions. Model grading uses another model as judge. Human raters and CJE-style calibration of judges against oracles are first-class. ISO/IEC TR 29119-11 highlights the oracle problem when expected results are hard to specify. Refusals may be logged separately from task success.

questions.text: Which scorer or judge configuration produced each sample score, including grader model, rubric, and whether scoring was live or deferred and later re-scored?
For each sample, what were the input, output, target, score value, explanation and refusal or scanner flags?
If a model or crowd judge was used, what agreement with gold oracles, inter-rater reliability and bias controls support treating those judgments as evidence?
Do sample inputs, outputs or rater notes contain personal data or prohibited content, and what minimization or redaction applies?

data_elements.name: Sample identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of an evaluated item within the run.

data_elements.name: Score value
data_elements.description: Numeric, boolean or categorical score emitted by the scorer.

data_elements.name: Grader model identifier
data_elements.description: Model used as judge when scoring is model-graded.

data_elements.name: Refusal flag
data_elements.description: Whether the subject refused rather than attempting the task.

artifacts.name: Sample score table
artifacts.description: Per-sample inputs, outputs, targets, scores, explanations and scanner flags, possibly reduced across epochs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Run master identifier plus sample identifier; re-score produces a new score serial, not a new sample identity.

bundles.name: Results, findings and approval
bundles.description: Aggregation, uncertainty, findings against claims, limitations, gated decisions and post-market re-evaluation.
bundles.rationale: TEVV-Athlon Synthesize and Interrogate turns block evidence into organizational decisions and feeds Manage. AI RMF requires documented TEVV, uncertainty and go or no-go decisions. EU Article 15 requires lifecycle-consistent accuracy and robustness; Articles 43, 55 and 72 consume evaluation evidence for conformity, GPAI systemic-risk evaluation and post-market monitoring.

layers.name: Results and findings
layers.description: Aggregate metrics, uncertainty, subgroup slices, findings and incompleteness disclosures.

findings.name: Aggregate results and uncertainty
findings.description: Inspect EvalResults hold scorer metrics; reductions handle multi-epoch scores; clustered standard errors are supported. ISO/IEC TS 4213 adds paired t-tests, ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis for significance. HELM reports head-to-head and trade-offs. Baselines and comparison sets must be named. NIST warns that measurement must include uncertainty and that Goodhart's law threatens metric targets.

questions.text: What aggregate metric values were obtained for each metric and subgroup slice, including sample size and missingness?
What interval, standard error or significance-test result accompanies each aggregate, and against which baseline or champion was the comparison made?
Which metric trade-offs (for example accuracy versus robustness or toxicity) are material, and were they measured in the same scenario?
Is this result set draft, final, corrected or retracted, and what errata supersede earlier published numbers?

data_elements.name: Aggregate metric value
data_elements.description: Reduced metric for a run or campaign slice.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty object
data_elements.description: Interval, clustered standard error or significance-test payload.

data_elements.name: Baseline identifier
data_elements.description: Comparison system or chance baseline required by ISO/IEC TS 4213.

artifacts.name: Aggregate results table
artifacts.description: Metric-by-slice results with uncertainty, baselines and result state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Run or campaign master identifier plus results serial; leaderboard rank is not an identifier.

findings.name: Evaluation finding
findings.description: A finding is an atomic, reviewable conclusion that a claim is supported, refuted or inconclusive given named evidence, including limitations. HELM requires explicit listing of missing scenarios and metrics. TEVV-Athlon Stage 4 synthesizes what occurred in each event as evidence for blocks. Subject-matter experts should interpret TEVV findings against deployment conditions.

questions.text: For each claim, is the verdict support, refute or inconclusive, and which result rows and sample exhibits constitute the evidence?
What limitations, missing scenarios, distribution shift and construct gaps must be disclosed with the finding?
Who authored, reviewed and approved the finding, and from which run logs was it derived?
If the finding arises from red-team or adversarial events, is publication restricted because it discloses exploitable vulnerabilities?

data_elements.name: Finding identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of an atomic evaluation finding.

data_elements.name: Verdict
data_elements.description: Support, refute or inconclusive relative to a claim.

data_elements.name: Limitations disclosure
data_elements.description: Known incompleteness and construct gaps.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Publication and sharing constraint, especially for red-team results.

artifacts.name: Evaluation finding record
artifacts.description: Atomic finding with verdict, evidence links, limitations and sensitivity class.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative finding identifier from the evaluation or risk platform of record, then IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Approval and monitoring
layers.description: Gates that consume findings, and triggers that force re-evaluation over the system lifecycle.

findings.name: Gate approval decision
findings.description: AI RMF effectiveness includes explicit go or no-go commissioning. EU conformity assessment (Article 43, Annexes VI and VII) and GPAI systemic-risk evaluation (Article 55) consume documented tests. Notified bodies may repeat tests and, as a last resort, access models. A decision is not a metric; it is an authorized act with a recorded owner.

questions.text: Was the gate outcome go, no-go, conditional deploy or waive, against which claims and findings, and what conditions attach?
Which role or notified body had authority to decide, and was a third-party or internal-control procedure used?
When was the decision made as event time, and when was it recorded in the register as observation time?
Which evaluation logs, metric declarations and technical-documentation excerpts were in the evidence pack at decision time?

data_elements.name: Decision identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of the gate decision.

data_elements.name: Decision code
data_elements.description: Go, no-go, conditional or waive.

data_elements.name: Decision authority
data_elements.description: Accountable person, body or notified body.

data_elements.name: Decided at
data_elements.description: Event time of the decision, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

artifacts.name: Approval or gate record
artifacts.description: Authorized decision with evidence pack, conditions, procedure and timestamps.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative decision identifier in the deployer or notified-body register, then IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Re-evaluation and post-market monitoring
findings.description: AI RMF requires regular TEVV and tracking of emergent risks. EU Article 15 requires consistent accuracy and robustness throughout the lifecycle and mitigation of biased feedback loops for systems that keep learning. Article 72 requires a post-market monitoring plan. Model or data changes, incidents, threshold breaches and scheduled cadence are typical triggers.

questions.text: Which events (subject version change, data drift, incident, scheduled cadence, threshold breach, regulatory request) trigger a new campaign or run?
If the system continues to learn after deployment, what evaluation detects biased feedback loops and what mitigation is required before continued operation?
Has a market-surveillance authority, AI Office or scientific panel requested or conducted an evaluation of this subject, and what access was granted?
What post-market monitoring plan identifiers, metrics and reporting frequency apply to this deployed subject?

data_elements.name: Re-evaluation trigger type
data_elements.description: Coded reason a new evaluation is required.

data_elements.name: Continual learning flag
data_elements.description: Whether the subject learns after placement on the market.

data_elements.name: Post-market monitoring plan identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the Article 72 or analogous monitoring plan.

artifacts.name: Post-market evaluation monitoring plan
artifacts.description: Plan of metrics, cadence, triggers and reporting for deployed systems.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Monitoring-plan identifier in the provider's quality system; linked to subject artifact identifier.

bundles.name: Stewardship and interoperability
bundles.description: Ownership, access, retention, deletion, reproducibility packaging and alignments that let another party re-run or audit an evaluation.
bundles.rationale: Inspect logs are URIs with optional S3 conditional writes and post-eval edits that track provenance. Croissant and PROV-O record dataset lineage. EU documentation-keeping and log obligations constrain retention. Reproducibility requires enough of dataset pin, subject pin, adaptation, environment and scorer to re-execute, which closed models may not allow.

layers.name: Access, retention and interoperability
layers.description: Who may see logs and findings, how long they are kept, and how a campaign is exchanged.

findings.name: Access, retention and reproducibility
findings.description: Eval logs may contain prompts, outputs, images, model-API payloads and PII. Inspect supports refusing image logging and restricting model-API logging. Red-team findings may be non-public. Reproducibility packages pin dataset hashes, subject versions, task specs and scorer versions; they are not the same as publishing the full log. Interoperability is alignment to Croissant, EvalLog semantics and declared metrics, not a claim of universal schema conformance.

questions.text: Who may read campaign metadata, sample-level logs, red-team findings and approval records, and which default-deny exceptions exist?
What retention period, legal hold and deletion or redaction method apply to logs, rater data and personal data in samples?
What pinned dataset hashes, subject versions, task specs, seeds and scorer versions are required to re-run, and which of those cannot be released because the subject is closed?
How is integrity of the run log and any post-eval score or tag edits guaranteed, including hashes, etags and provenance of log updates?
Which party owns the evaluation records and which accountable deployer must be able to produce them to an authority?

data_elements.name: Access policy
data_elements.description: Role-to-scope mapping for campaign, findings, artifacts and sample logs.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or rule for keeping evaluation records.

data_elements.name: Reproducibility package identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the pin-set sufficient for attempted re-run.

data_elements.name: Log content hash
data_elements.description: Integrity hash of the canonical run log.

artifacts.name: Reproducibility package
artifacts.description: Pinned subject, dataset, task, scorer, environment and hashes needed to attempt a re-run, with an explicit list of unreleased closed components.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Package identifier derived from campaign and run master identifiers plus content hash; not a date.

functions.name: Plan evaluation campaign
functions.description: Create a campaign with goal, claims, class, independence model and intended events, corresponding to TEVV-Athlon Articulate and Organize plus Define and Construct.
preconditions: Subject artifact identifier exists in WM-SFT-004 or an equivalent register
effects: Gate rule and declared metrics are versioned

functions.name: Bind evaluation dataset and splits
functions.description: Pin a dataset version, split, hashes and field map for evaluation use without mutating WM-AI-009 master data, and record leakage controls.
preconditions: Test split is not used as training data for the subject under this campaign
effects: Campaign holds an immutable pin of evaluation data as used

functions.name: Execute evaluation run
functions.description: Run tasks against the pinned subject and dataset in a specified environment and write a run log.
preconditions: Campaign is planned or in execution
Sandbox policy is accepted for agentic tasks
effects: Samples, model events and usage stats are recorded
Partial or error status is first-class

functions.name: Score and aggregate
functions.description: Apply scorers or judges, optionally deferred or re-scored, reduce epochs and compute metrics with uncertainty.
preconditions: Run status is success or a declared partial-run policy applies
effects: Metrics become evidence for metrology blocks
Re-score creates a new score serial linked to the same samples

functions.name: Scan evaluation integrity
functions.description: Review transcripts for refusals, evaluation awareness, leakage, harness failure and other threats to validity.
effects: Validity exceptions are attached to samples or the run

functions.name: Issue evaluation finding
functions.description: Synthesize block evidence into claim-level verdicts with limitations, corresponding to TEVV-Athlon Synthesize and Interrogate.
preconditions: Results state is final or a draft-finding policy is declared
effects: Findings become reviewable evidence for Manage and for gates

functions.name: Decide evaluation gate
functions.description: Apply the authorized go, no-go, conditional or waive rule to findings and record the decision with an evidence pack.
preconditions: Independence and procedure requirements for the risk class are met
effects: Subject may be commissioned, blocked, conditionally deployed or waived
Decision event time and recording time are stored

functions.name: Package reproducibility evidence
functions.description: Assemble pins, hashes and unreleased-component list so another party can attempt a re-run or audit.
preconditions: Content hashes for released components exist
effects: A serial package is linked to the campaign and runs

functions.name: Trigger re-evaluation
functions.description: Open a new campaign or run when monitoring triggers fire, including continual-learning feedback-loop risks and official evaluation requests.
preconditions: A monitoring plan or legal duty to re-evaluate exists
effects: Prior approval may be marked stale pending new findings

composition.purpose: Bind a versioned benchmark or evaluation dataset, split and integrity metadata into a campaign without owning dataset-master semantics.
Identify the model or system artifact version and interface that is the subject under evaluation.

composition.target: NIST AI RMF Measure and TEVV-Athlon
composition.purpose: Treat this aggregate as the Measure implementation: campaigns, blocks, events, tools, findings and go or no-go evidence feeding Manage. Alignment is not a claim of RMF certification.

Reuse control criteria, confusion-matrix metrics, environment documentation, baselines and significance tests when the task is classification. Do not claim 4213 coverage of generative, agentic or benchmark-suite evaluation.

Support declared accuracy metrics, lifecycle-consistent performance, dataset split discipline, conformity evidence, GPAI systemic-risk evaluation and post-market monitoring where those legal duties apply. Alignment is not a declaration of conformity.
Use Croissant dataset, split, hash and PROV-O properties when describing evaluation-time dataset bindings.
Reuse scenario (task, domain, language), standardized adaptation and multi-metric-in-context measurement, including explicit incompleteness.
Align run, sample, score, reduction and status semantics with Inspect without making JSON or .eval files the model.

owner_package_requirements: AI system owner and accountable deployer named as record owner and decision authority for operational evaluations
Independent validator or TEVV function separated from model builders, with documented conflicts when separation is incomplete
Evaluation-platform-of-record identifier scheme for campaigns, runs, metrics, findings and decisions
Quality-management linkage so declared metrics and post-market monitoring plans can be produced to an authority
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint campaign, run, metric, finding and decision identifiers in a Dimension-owned namespace. Prefer the evaluation platform of record as master. When publishing, mint IRIs; Croissant IRIs apply only to bound datasets. Do not use dates, leaderboard ranks or metric values as identifiers.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical evaluation objects are campaign, dataset-binding, metric, task-spec, run, sample-score, aggregate-result, finding and decision; file formats are projections
Metric identifiers are stable; a formula change allocates a new metric identifier rather than silently mutating history
Closed-model API strings are recorded as interface identifiers, not as substitutes for missing weight hashes
Timestamps canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z
patch_rules: Post-eval score edits, tag edits and finding errata are append-only patches with actor and time, matching Inspect log_updates provenance
Re-scoring creates a new score serial linked to the same sample identifiers
Retracted results remain readable to auditors with a superseded-by pointer
Threshold or gate-rule changes do not rewrite historical decisions
compatibility_rules: A run remains comparable only if subject version, dataset pin, adaptation protocol and metric identifiers match
Partial runs must not be mixed with complete runs in an aggregate without an explicit missingness rule
ISO/IEC TS 4213 metric names may be used only when the task is classification and the formula matches
Draft NIST AI 200-2 TEVV-Athlon terms are optional annotations until that document is finalized

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the evaluation platform of record (campaign ID, run ID, finding ID or decision ID)
Governed global identifier or IRI when the Dimension publishes the object
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or IRI exists
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record every evaluation timestamp in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Distinguish event time (when inference, scoring, a human judgment, or a gate decision occurred) from observation or ingestion time (when the evaluation store received the record); when those differ, store both.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serials version plans, metric specs, score tables, findings and approval records under a stable object identifier; serial numbers are not identities and must not embed calendar dates as the object ID.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Canonical run logs and released reproducibility packages carry a content hash; dataset FileObjects use sha256 when Croissant metadata exists; remote stores should use conditional writes (for example if-match etag) so post-eval edits cannot silently clobber another writer's log.

policies: Do not treat a single accuracy number as a complete evaluation; record absent metric classes and coverage gaps
Keep builders and validators separated for high-risk or systemic-risk subjects unless a documented exception applies
Do not use test-split items in training or prompt-tuning of the subject under the same campaign
Red-team and vulnerability findings default to restricted access
Human-subjects or field tests require documented consent and ethics approval before execution
Metric targets are reviewed for Goodhart effects before they become gate rules

read: Campaign metadata readable to the owner, validators and authorized auditors
Sample-level logs readable only under the sample-log policy
Red-team findings readable only to the declared sharing circle
Public leaderboard projections contain aggregates only, never raw prompts that the license forbids
create: Campaigns created by the evaluation owner or delegated designer
Runs created only against pinned subject and dataset bindings
Findings created from final or explicitly draft results
Decisions created only by the named authority
update: Re-score and scanner patches append to the run; they do not rewrite sample identity
Finding errata supersede; they do not delete the original finding
Campaign state transitions are recorded with event time
Tags and metadata updates carry provenance
delete: Deletion of logs containing personal data follows the retention rule and legal hold
Redaction is preferred to physical delete when an approval evidence pack still depends on the run
Withdrawn campaigns are marked withdrawn, not silently removed
Accountable deployers must retain evidence required by applicable documentation-keeping duties before any delete

roles.name: AI system owner and accountable deployer
responsibilities: Own gate decisions and residual-risk acceptance
Produce evaluation evidence to authorities when required

roles.name: Evaluation designer
responsibilities: Write goals, claims, blocks, events, tasks and metric specifications
Disclose coverage gaps and construct-validity arguments
Keep adaptation protocols standardized across compared subjects

roles.name: Independent validator
responsibilities: Execute or witness runs without builder control of scores
Refuse to certify when leakage, oracle or independence controls fail

roles.name: Dataset steward
responsibilities: Maintain the WM-AI-009 pin, license constraints and split hygiene
Authorize evaluation-time use and output publication rules

roles.name: Rater or judge
responsibilities: Report conflicts, fatigue and personal-data issues in items

roles.name: Notified body or official evaluator
responsibilities: Perform or repeat tests under a legal conformity or Article 92-style mandate
Record access granted to models or training data as a last-resort verification step

access.default_rule: Default deny on sample-level logs, model-API payloads, red-team exhibits and personal data; campaign-level aggregates may be wider according to license and owner policy.
exceptions: Break-glass auditor or market-surveillance access with recorded legal basis
Notified-body or AI-Office evaluation access under a documented request
Public aggregate leaderboards when the dataset license and sensitivity class allow
Internal builder debugging of failed runs without permission to edit scores
audit_requirements: Append-only provenance for score edits, tag edits, finding errata and decisions
Retention of evidence packs for the documentation-keeping period applicable to the subject
Record of who accessed restricted red-team findings

coverage.claim: This aggregate is a defensible, format-neutral context structure for AI model and system evaluation as a campaign of datasets-as-used, metrics, runs, findings and approvals, grounded in NIST TEVV and AI RMF Measure, ISO/IEC TS 4213 controls, EU accuracy and monitoring duties, Croissant dataset pins, Inspect run semantics and HELM multi-metric practice. It is not a universal evaluation ontology and does not claim conformance to those instruments.

checklist.notes: Campaign, run, metric, sample, finding and decision identifiers with master-system first, then IRI, then UUID or ULID.
Campaign and run states, re-score serials, go or no-go, withdrawal, stale approval and re-evaluation triggers.
Typed references to WM-AI-009 datasets and WM-SFT-004 subjects, plus scorer, baseline and evidence-pack links.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion times for runs, scores, scans and decisions; live versus frozen dataset snapshots.
Label authorship, Croissant or PROV-O dataset lineage, log-update trails, finding authors and reproducibility pins.
Record owner, accountable deployer, builder versus validator separation and dataset steward.
Construct validation, leakage and contamination controls, oracle definition, integrity scanners and significance plans.
Default-deny sample logs and red-team exhibits; official-evaluator exceptions; public aggregates.
Retention period, legal hold, redaction versus delete, documentation-keeping duties.
Alignments to Croissant, Inspect EvalLog, HELM, ISO/IEC TS 4213 and EU declared metrics without format lock-in.
Metric formulae, multi-metric sets, uncertainty, slices, baselines and computational metrics from ISO/IEC TS 4213.
Inspect model grading, human raters, IRR and oracle calibration; ethics approval for field tests.
Gate decisions, internal-control versus notified-body paths, GPAI evaluation and post-market plans as alignments.
Split leakage, canaries, evaluation awareness and Goodhart risk on metric gates.

known_omissions: ISO/IEC 24029 formal and statistical robustness methods are neighboring techniques not modelled in full; primary text was not retrieved beyond catalogue scope lines.
ISO/IEC TS 42119-2:2025 testing-of-AI overview and the in-progress ISO/IEC CD 4213 expansion to regression, clustering and recommendation were not retrieved as full text.
ISO/IEC 25059 AI quality model, ISO/IEC 42001 AIMS audit evidence and ISO/IEC DIS 24970 AI logging are not encoded.
MLPerf, Hugging Face Evaluate, OpenAI Evals and EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness schemas are widely used projections not treated as canonical.
Model Cards (Mitchell et al.) and data cards are reporting formats; only finding and results artifacts are modelled here.
Medical-device, aviation and SR 11-7-style financial model-validation regimes are out of scope and unmapped.
China, sectoral and other non-EU, non-US evaluation statutes were not searched in this pass.
Inter-laboratory reproducibility protocols and energy-measurement metrology beyond ISO/IEC TS 4213 mentions remain thin.
Human-subjects statistical-power design for ARIA-style contextual evaluations is only pointed at via TEVV-Athlon field-testing tools.
conflicts: ISO/IEC TS 4213 explicitly excludes benchmarking and use cases, while HELM, Inspect and TEVV-Athlon are built around scenarios, suites and events; this model aligns to both and must not claim 4213 conformance for generative or agentic suites.
Single-score leaderboards conflict with HELM multi-metric-in-context measurement and with NIST's Goodhart warning.
First-party vendor evals conflict with AI RMF separation of builders from validators and with EU notified-body testing.
Model-as-judge scores conflict with gold-label oracles; both are allowed only when judge quality is recorded.
NIST AI 200-2 is an initial public draft (comment period open as of August 2026) overlapping a published AI RMF 1.0; TEVV-Athlon terms are therefore provisional.
Closed-model API evaluation cannot satisfy bit-level reproducibility required by Croissant file hashes for the subject itself.
EU Article 15 'appropriate' accuracy is legal and context-dependent; ISO/IEC TS 4213 metrics are statistical and classification-specific.
regional_assumptions: EU Articles 10, 15, 43, 55, 72 and 92 apply to providers and deployers in the Union for in-scope systems and GPAI models; they are alignments, not global duties.
NIST AI RMF and TEVV-Athlon are voluntary US measurement frameworks, not binding law.
UK AISI Inspect and the Autonomous Systems Evaluation Standard are de facto frontier-evaluation engineering practice, not a statute.
Croissant adoption is concentrated in Hugging Face, Kaggle and OpenML ecosystems and is not universal.
Classification-performance controls in ISO/IEC TS 4213 are assumed transferable as hygiene controls (leakage, environment, baselines) even when the metric set does not apply.
adversarial_checks: Checked that evaluation datasets-as-used are bindings rather than a second dataset-master model competing with WM-AI-009.
Checked that the subject under evaluation is a reference to WM-SFT-004 plus interface configuration, not a duplicate model-card identity.
Checked that JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are treated as projections, with Inspect .eval and .json called out as such.
Checked that dates are not used as identifiers and that event time is separated from ingestion time.
Checked that rare paths (partial runs, re-score, retraction, red-team non-publication, continual-learning feedback loops, official evaluations, field-test consent) are present or listed as omissions.
Checked that no node claims universal completeness; ISO 24029, 42119-2, Model Cards and non-Western law are explicit gaps.
